origin.description: time<- on a plain zoo checks the length and then stores the index, sorted or not. On a zooreg it uses the same replacement as index<-, including the frequency check.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An object. A zoo series stores observations separately from its index.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: A new index of the same length. A plain zoo does not require it to be sorted.

origin.details: time<- on a plain zoo checks the length and then stores the index, sorted or not. On a zooreg it uses the same replacement as index<-, including the frequency check.
origin.value: The series with the new index.
origin.example:
x <- zoo(1:3, 1:3)
time(x) <- c(3, 1, 2)
cat(paste(index(x), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")

translation.example:
import numpy as np
from zoo.series import Zoo
from zoo.index import index, time_set
x = time_set(Zoo(np.arange(1, 4), [1, 2, 3]), [3, 1, 2])
print(" ".join(str(int(v)) for v in index(x)))
